sections.overview: The megamouth is a large, rarely encountered oceanic filter-feeding shark and the only living member of its genus.
sections.identification: Its unusually broad head and large terminal mouth distinguish it from most sharks, and the largest reported individuals approach eight to nine metres.
sections.habitat: It ranges widely through tropical and warm-temperate oceans, from near the surface to about fifteen hundred metres, with many records from Japan, Taiwan and the Philippines.
sections.diet: It filter-feeds on planktonic animals, including krill, taking small drifting prey from the water.
sections.behavior: Tagging and capture records suggest vertical movements that may follow prey migrating between depths during day and night.
sections.reproduction: Reproduction is poorly documented; the species is thought to bear live young nourished by yolk, while uterine cannibalism remains uncertain.
sections.ecology: Off Taiwan, it has been recorded as bycatch in a fishery targeting sharptail mola (Masturus lanceolatus); see that profile for the reciprocal link.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment published in 2019 classified it as Least Concern but recommended monitoring catches because it is rare and potentially sensitive to overexploitation.
